dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Poultry skewer with BBQ sauce, salty grilled fish, kitsune ramen... Dear customer, how would you like to try some native Inazuma snacks?

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: We also serve tea. We have genmaicha, barley, and oolong. Which one would you like? We do not serve alcohol, though.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Hmm, odd, is it? Well, think about it. If you drink too much, your taste buds will get numb, and you won't be able to taste how good the dishes are anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: So even if most Inazuman snacks go well with alcohol, we don't serve alcohol here.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: To me, the bitterness and the aftertaste of tea can bring out the taste of the skewers and the sauce better. Alcohol would just cover everything up.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Aside from the skewers, you might want to order some kitsune ramen if you want something more filling... Ah, by the way, you aren't allergic to beans, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: There was a case like this before, so it's better safe than sorry for me to ask first.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: There was once an Oni gentleman and a lady with kitsune ears who made a bet here on who could eat the most kitsune ramen.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: But there was fried tofu in the ramen, and the Oni people are allergic to beans...

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Therefore, even though that gentleman with long horns won the bet, he also almost lost his life... Was it worthwhile?

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Take care. Come back again next time.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: I see. You aren't old enough to drink, right? That's also fine. You can order some tea while savoring some of Inazuma's snacks.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Here, these Onigiri are freshly made today. They are delicious and filling. Please have some.
